title: Self-help diagnostics: which admin tests explain a broken setting, and who can run them?
summary: The diagnostic locations, permissions, commands and Microsoft 365 admin center data-handling statements are supported by Microsoft documentation. Minor corrections are needed to name the Graph role-assignment body properties, cite the status-view examples and use the standard wording for unpublished licensing.

claims.claim: Self-help diagnostics are administrator-run tests of tenant and user configuration to explain problems.
claims.quote: You can run diagnostics to identify and resolve issues in Microsoft Purview.

claims.where: controls[4].ui; What it is: Where they run
claims.claim: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, open Help, describe the issue, select an option and select Run Tests.
claims.quote:
Select the Help icon in the upper-right corner of the portal to open the Help pane.
Select one of the listed options that are generated based on the issue that you described.
If the selected option has an associated diagnostic, enter any requested information, and then select Run Tests

claims.where: What it is: Where they run, Microsoft Purview portal Help pane
claims.claim: In the Purview portal, Help then Ask a question opens the diagnostic search experience.
claims.quote:
Open the Help and support pane: Select the Help icon in the upper-right corner of the portal.
Open the Help pane: In the Help and support pane, select Ask a question.

claims.claim: Text analytics of the problem description surfaces matching Help-pane diagnostics.
claims.quote: Describe the problem that you want to resolve, and the appropriate diagnostics are surfaced through text analytics of the problem description.

claims.claim: A Help-pane diagnostic requests the information needed before it runs.
claims.quote: If the selected option has an associated diagnostic, enter any requested information, and then select Run Tests to start the diagnostic.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center diagnostics take inputs such as a user name, URL or meeting ID.
claims.quote: To run a diagnostic, administrators provide specific values that are needed to troubleshoot an issue, such as a user name, URL, or Meeting ID.

claims.claim: Microsoft uses supplied values to gather additional configuration data scoped to them.
claims.quote: Microsoft uses this information to gather additional data that is scoped to those values. This data can be tenant-defined, user-defined, or system-defined configuration information.

claims.claim: A Solutions-page diagnostic first runs Check-PurviewConfig and then the issue-specific cmdlet.
claims.quote: the diagnostic runs the Check-PurviewConfig cmdlet to check your organization's configuration settings in Microsoft Purview. Then, the diagnostic calls the appropriate cmdlet that's listed in the following table to perform checks that are specific to your issue.

claims.claim: The email-encryption diagnostic uses Test-IrmConfiguration.
claims.quote:
Email encryption isn't working as expected. Are there any issues that affect my licenses or settings?
Verifies encryption settings. | Test-IrmConfiguration

claims.claim: The missing-label diagnostic uses Get-Label.
claims.quote: A user can't find the sensitivity label they need. Does the label policy apply to them? | Checks which sensitivity labels are available to the user. Diagnostic results include information such as the label names, settings, and where the labels are available. | Get-label Get-LabelPolicy

claims.claim: The missing-label diagnostic uses Get-LabelPolicy.
claims.quote: A user can't find the sensitivity label they need. Does the label policy apply to them? | Checks which sensitivity labels are available to the user. Diagnostic results include information such as the label names, settings, and where the labels are available. | Get-label Get-LabelPolicy

claims.claim: The SharePoint or OneDrive DLP file diagnostic uses Test-DlpPolicies.
claims.quote:
A DLP rule isn't triggering for a file stored in SharePoint or OneDrive. Is the file evaluated by DLP, and is it in scope for the policy?
Test-DlpPolices

claims.claim: The SharePoint or OneDrive auto-labeling file diagnostic uses Test-DlpPolicies.
claims.quote:
Autolabeling isn't applied to a SharePoint or OneDrive file. Was the file evaluated correctly, and did it meet the autolabeling conditions?
Test-DlpPolices

claims.claim: DLP diagnostics accept an uploaded message trace log to review rules applied to Exchange Online messages.
claims.quote: A DLP rule didn't apply or it was applied unexpectedly to an email message in Exchange Online. | Upload the message trace log (.csv) to review the DLP rules applied to email messages.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Data leaves the compliance boundary briefly
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center diagnostics show a consent notice for temporary processing and storage of tenant and user configuration outside the compliance boundary.
claims.quote: When you run a self-help diagnostic in the Microsoft 365 admin center, a consent notice informs you that tenant and user configuration information will be processed and stored temporarily outside the compliance boundary.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Data leaves the compliance boundary briefly
claims.claim: Configuration data retrieved can include display names, email subject lines and SharePoint site names.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Data leaves the compliance boundary briefly
claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center diagnostic service never accesses customer content such as messages and documents.
claims.quote: Customer content such as email messages, documents, and chat conversations is never accessed by the diagnostic service.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Data leaves the compliance boundary briefly
claims.claim: Microsoft automatically removes the processed data after the Microsoft 365 admin center diagnostic finishes.
claims.quote: The data that the support systems process is automatically removed after the diagnostic process is finished. This data isn't retained for use beyond the scope of the specific diagnostic that you run.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document a tenant setting to switch self-help diagnostics off.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview self-help diagnostics disable restrict tenant admin setting. Opened: Self-help diagnostics for Microsoft Purview; Self-help diagnostics for issues in Exchange Online and Outlook; Permissions in the Microsoft Purview portal. No diagnostic off-switch found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licence requirement specifically for running self-help diagnostics.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 self-help diagnostics licensing price running diagnostics. Read: Purview and Exchange self-help diagnostic pages; Test your Data Loss Prevention policies; Microsoft Purview service-description search excerpt. No licence specifically for diagnostic runs found.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence with: 'At the time of writing (November 2026), Microsoft has not published a licence requirement or charge specifically for running self-help diagnostics: Not yet published.'

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a charge specifically for running self-help diagnostics.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 self-help diagnostics licensing price running diagnostics; Microsoft 365 Purview self-help diagnostics disable tenant setting opt out licence pricing charge. Read Purview diagnostics, Exchange diagnostics and DLP testing; no charge for diagnostic runs found.

claims.claim: Purview role-group members are added at Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users.
claims.quote:
Go to Settings > Roles and scopes
Select Role groups.
On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select a Microsoft Purview role group you want to add users to. Select Edit on the control bar.
On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member <member> adds a member to a role group.
claims.quote:
Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group.
The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to.
The Member parameter specifies who you want to add to the role group.

claims.claim: Managing Purview role-group membership in the portal requires the Role management role.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal by using credentials for an admin account assigned the Role management role.

claims.claim: Directory administrator roles can be assigned at Microsoft 365 admin center > Roles > Role assignments > Microsoft Entra ID > role > Assigned > Add users.
claims.quote:
go to Roles > Role assignments.
choose the Microsoft Entra ID, Exchange, Intune, or Billing tab.
Select the administrator role that you want to assign the user to.
On the Assigned tab, select Add users or Add groups.

claims.claim: For delegated work or school access, Privileged Role Administrator is the least privileged supported built-in role for creating a directory role assignment.

claims.quote: Use the Invoke-ProvisioningCompanyObjectDiagnostic cmdlet to validate and fix core Microsoft 365 tenant information and service plan configuration in cloud-based organizations.
